## Register and classify block faces (`boundary-condition/external/*`) {#sec-ch11-registry}

### Summary

Every boundary callback is a function of a tensor, a dimension and a `BoundaryFuncOptions` context, entered
into one global registry under its name by the `BC_FUNCTION` macro ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.hpp BC_FUNCTION >}}),
which also declares the contract a callback must keep: it may be called again on a thin tangential ghost slab
after an exchange, so it must not depend on the orthogonal extent of its input and a second call must
reproduce the first. The card names a callback per face; `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml` appends `_inner`
or `_outer`, looks the name up in the registry, and refuses a name that is not there. Construction of the block
then nulls the callbacks of the faces that another block or a periodic wrap supplies, so that "physical face"
and "callback present" mean the same thing from then on.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Maps the six face names of the YAML card to registered callbacks, drops the callbacks on the
faces the layout owns, and classifies a face when an operator asks whether it is physical or a wall.

**Switch.** `boundary-condition/external/x1-inner` ... `x3-outer`; each defaults to `reflecting`.

**Requires / implies / turns off.** A periodic x2 or x3 face sets the layout's periodic flag; a periodic x1 face
does so only on the `cubed` layout. A layout-owned face has no callback.

**Order.** Dispatch only; no order of accuracy.

**Defining equation.** None; the two predicates are stated in the Derivation layer.
:::

### Derivation

This is dispatch infrastructure, so there is no differential equation to discretize. Two predicates carry the
chapter. A face is *physical* exactly when its callback is non-null: `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_physical_boundary`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_physical_boundary >}}) tests the entry of
`bfuncs` at the face index that `face_of` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp face_of >}}) returns, first
match winning in x3, x2, x1 order. A face is a *diffusion wall* when it is physical and its recorded name is one
of `reflecting_inner`, `reflecting_outer`, `fixed_temperature_inner` or `fixed_temperature_outer`:
`MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary >}})
is a whitelist, and a physical face whose name was not recorded (a callback installed programmatically without
a name) warns once and is not a wall. The hydro predicate `HydroImpl::is_x1_wall`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::is_x1_wall >}}) is a third, different set: a physical x1 face whose
name does not start with `periodic`. The three sets are nested but not equal: an outflow face is physical and
an x1 wall for the hydro, but not a diffusion wall; an in-block periodic x1 face (slab layout) is physical but
neither kind of wall.

A repeated fill must reproduce the same ghost values from the owned slab. This idempotence is a contract on the
callback, not a property of every tensor map; the registry asks for it because the corner refresh of
@sec-ch11-timing calls the x1 callbacks a second time on a slab that is only $n_g$ cells wide in the
tangential direction. Check C1 exercises the contract for the built-in mirror and copy rules; no spatial order
is assigned to dispatch [check `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`]. The checks do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The face order is x1 inner, x1 outer, x2 inner, x2 outer, x3 inner, x3 outer (`BoundaryFace`,
{{< code src/bc/bc.hpp BoundaryFace >}}); in the four-dimensional hydro tensor `(variable, x3, x2, x1)` these
faces act on dimensions 3, 2 and 1, and a callback receives the dimension it fills. The context
`BoundaryFuncOptions` ({{< code src/bc/bc.hpp BoundaryFuncOptions >}}) carries a non-owning EOS and coordinate
pointer, the saved backgrounds that outflow needs, the representation (`kConserved`, `kPrimitive` or
`kScalar`) and the ghost width $n_g$. On a collapsed direction (one cell) the card entry is not read: the
parser pushes a null callback and an empty name for both faces of that direction whenever a later direction
has more than one cell, so the face indices of the other directions stay in place.

`MeshBlockImpl::reset` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}) nulls, for a slab or cubed
layout, the callback of every face that has a neighbouring block in that direction or whose direction is
periodic in the layout; the cubed-sphere layout keeps its own panel rules and is not touched by this step. A
non-null custom callback therefore still counts as physical for every predicate above. No accuracy order
follows from classification.

: Implementation sites for registry. {#tbl-ch11-registry-code}

1. Validate the keys under `boundary-condition` and `boundary-condition/external`, read each face name with
   the default `reflecting`, append `_inner` or `_outer`, and reject a name absent from the registry. A
   periodic x2 or x3 name sets `periodic_x` or `periodic_y`; a periodic x1 name sets `periodic_z` only when
   the layout type is `cubed`. The anchor `periodic_z` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}.
2. At construction, null the callbacks of the faces the layout owns. The anchor `bfuncs` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}.
3. Classify at the consuming operator: `is_physical_boundary` for the hydro, the exchange and the implicit
   solve; `is_wall_boundary` for diffusion, where an unnamed callback warns once and returns false. The anchor
   `is_wall_boundary` is in {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_wall_boundary >}}.

{{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp yaml_keys.boundary_condition_refuses_an_unknown_key >}} and

The rest assertions are `EXPECT_LE` on the Mach number in
{{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.x2_uniform_rest_keeps_u2_zero >}} and
{{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.user_wall_keeps_u2_zero >}}.

Numeric tolerances above are the source test constants; a round-off derivation is not documented for each.
Device/rank distinctions and missing runs are recorded in @sec-ch15-ch11.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The fixed-temperature names are accepted by the diffusion whitelist, but the boundary sources at the pin
register no callback under them, so the card cannot select a thermal wall. The comment above the whitelist
describes the outflow ghost as a zero-gradient statement, while the outflow callback of @sec-ch11-outflow
builds a characteristic state; the classification itself (not a wall) is unaffected. A cubed-sphere panel
face that carries a custom callback counts as physical wherever a physical-face test is used.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
